name: Aztec Camera
label: Rough Trade
lede: Roddy Frame was 16 when Postcard signed his band and 18 when Rough Trade put out High Land, Hard Rain. He spent the next twelve years under the Aztec Camera name chasing Knopfler, Jam and Lewis, Mick Jones and Ryuichi Sakamoto, and never made the same record twice.

hero.by: Roddy Frame in Los Angeles, 1987. Photo: Nancy J Price (Andwhatsnext), CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Sixteen and on Postcard
eras.text: Roddy Frame grew up in an East Kilbride council house playing guitar at lunchtime and again after school. Aztec Camera came out of the school band Neutral Blue, and inside a year Alan Horne's Postcard Records, home of Orange Juice and Josef K, had put out two of Frame's singles.

years.src: The Herald · Wikipedia: High Land, Hard Rain
years.h: Frame quits Neutral Blue and starts Aztec Camera
years.p: Frame forms the band in East Kilbride with drummer Dave Mulholland; [[Campbell Owens|66a25dad-5d09-4c09-8463-1dc74534500a]] replaces the first bassist, Alan Welsh, by the end of the year. Rehearsals are at The Key youth club.
years.xp: Neutral Blue had been a school-friends band with a set full of [[The Clash|8f92558c-2baa-4758-8c38-615519e9deda]] covers. Frame told Billy Sloan that hearing indie singles from Manchester and Sheffield, and then the Postcard bands in Glasgow, convinced him he could make a record too.

years.src: The Herald
years.h: The demo goes to Factory, Zoo and Rough Trade, but not Postcard
years.p: Cut at Sirocco Studios in Kilmarnock, the tape got the band a support slot with The Teardrop Explodes via Zoo, a pass from Factory and a polite rejection slip from Geoff Travis at Rough Trade.
years.xp: Frame skipped Postcard on purpose. He'd read an interview with label boss Alan Horne and decided "This guy hates everybody," so he saved the price of a stamp. After the session the band couldn't afford the trip back from Kilmarnock and walked home.

years.cap: Aztec Camera at Valentino's, Edinburgh, supporting Josef K
years.src: The Herald · Wikipedia: High Land, Hard Rain
years.h: Alan Horne, Edwyn Collins and Malcolm Ross stand at the front in Paisley
years.p: Opening for The Revillos at the Bungalow Bar, Frame plays with the Postcard boss and two of his stars heckling the bands right in front of him. Horne signs Aztec Camera days later.
years.xp: Billy Sloan was in the room that night. Frame was 16; the punk crowd was suspicious of jangly guitar pop, and Horne, [[Edwyn Collins|14c0c282-e0c1-46fe-acd1-9a015ba721c5]] and [[Malcolm Ross|649b6c50-f7da-4739-aa5e-e1c672474e84]] spent the night, in Frame's words, taking the piss out of everyone. Frame says this was the gig where Horne was deciding whether to sign them.

years.src: Wikipedia: Aztec Camera · Wikipedia: High Land, Hard Rain
years.h: Postcard puts out Just Like Gold
years.p: Frame's first single reaches No. 10 on the UK indie chart. Its B-side, We Could Send Letters, was written in 1979, when he was 15.
years.xp: An acoustic take on We Could Send Letters also turned up that year on C81, the cassette NME made with Rough Trade. Frame met Collins, then 21, during the Postcard days; the two stayed friends for decades.

years.h: Mattress of Wire climbs two places higher
years.p: The second Postcard single reaches No. 8 on the indie chart. A planned Postcard album, Green Jacket Grey, is shelved, and Mulholland leaves.

eras.title: Rough Trade's teenage songwriter
eras.text: Geoff Travis, who had turned down the demo, came back with a deal after hearing the Postcard singles. The band moved to London, picked up a drummer from The Ruts and made a debut at a Christian studio in Eastbourne that critics are still writing about forty years on.

years.h: London, a borrowed drummer, then [[Dave Ruffy|8b5cf309-3a53-4f6a-aa72-5460d077e4db]] of the Ruts
years.p: Blair Cunningham of Haircut One Hundred fills in before Ruffy takes the job; keyboardist Bernie Clarke joins soon after. Rough Trade signs them in the UK, Sire in the US.

years.h: Pillar to Post, the first Rough Trade single
years.p: Frame said he was aiming the song at the Clash and Tamla Motown at the same time. The B-side is The Queen's Tattoos.

years.cap: The High Land, Hard Rain line-up in Music Life
years.src: The Herald · Wikipedia: High Land, Hard Rain
years.h: A different guitar on every song at ICC, Eastbourne
years.p: Producer John Brand, who had engineered [[Magazine|043324ca-100d-48ce-8c7c-fd015afc103b]]'s Magic, Murder and the Weather, lets an 18-year-old run the room at International Christian Communication studio.
years.xp:
Frame told the Herald piles of guitars were lying around and he grabbed whichever fit: a funny little Gibson on Back on Board, a big Wes Montgomery jazz Gibson on Release. The backbone was a double-tracked Masano acoustic he'd owned for two months, the two takes slightly out of time with each other.

The album took three weeks. Frame liked the rush: "sometimes you can hear a bit of pressure in the album."

years.src: The Herald · Wikipedia: High Land, Hard Rain · Wikipedia: Aztec Camera
years.h: High Land, Hard Rain reaches No. 22
years.p: Ten songs written between the ages of 15 and 18, released on Rough Trade. It ends on Down the Dip, named for the Diplomat, a pub near Frame's old school, Duncanrig Secondary.
years.xp:
Frame wanted Back on Board to crossfade into Down the Dip, the last song he wrote for the record and just him and his guitar. Brand said try it. Glasgow artist David Band drew the sleeve.

In the New York Times, Jon Pareles heard folk-rock and wrote that the record might almost have been made 15 years earlier. It got to No. 129 on the Billboard 200.

years.cap: Lyceum, London, 15 March 1983, with the Farmers Boys and the Dainties
years.src: Wikipedia: High Land, Hard Rain · Wikipedia: Aztec Camera discography · Wikipedia: Aztec Camera
years.h: Second time out, Oblivious makes the Top 20
years.p: First released in January, it stalled at No. 47; the reissue reaches No. 18. Frame wrote it on purpose as a Top of the Pops song and lifted the guitar part from a [[Love|34ec9a8d-c65b-48fd-bcdd-aad2f72fdb47]] track.
years.xp: The borrowed riff is from Love's Maybe the People Would Be the Times or Between Clark and Hilldale. Frame later said being called a "boy" in the press annoyed him at the time: he was listening to [[Joy Division|9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd]] and taking it all very seriously.

years.h: [[Craig Gannon|856ee0fb-8378-4f59-9e42-365e8c7f7425]] plays guitar, then goes to [[The Smiths|40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27]]
years.p: Gannon is in Aztec Camera through 1984 before joining the Smiths, another Rough Trade band.

eras.title: Knopfler, Warners and the miners
eras.text: Frame signed to WEA at 18 without realizing the label would own his recordings. He went after Mark Knopfler as a producer, made a longer, glossier record, then took three years off and came back sounding like Minneapolis.

q: Here at Rough Trade we're not in the business of making stars.
A Rough Trade staffer, as Frame recalls
years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: Aztec Camera
years.h: Frame leaves Rough Trade for WEA
years.p: Frame's comeback, as he told the Quietus, when someone at Rough Trade said the label wasn't in the business of making stars. He felt his ideas were a little ahead of theirs.
years.xp: In a 2014 BBC radio interview Frame said nobody explained the ownership side of the WEA deal to him, and as an 18-year-old he hadn't understood that the company would own every recording he made for it. Manager Rob Johnson was running his affairs.

years.cap: Ticket for the Odeon, Birmingham, 10 October 1984
yt: Live at the Barrowland, Glasgow, August 1984
years.h: [[Malcolm Ross|649b6c50-f7da-4739-aa5e-e1c672474e84]], who watched from the front in Paisley, joins
years.p: Bernie Clarke leaves. Ross, formerly of [[Josef K|ab5f1b53-dabe-444a-a8fe-116cde87f709]] and Orange Juice, comes in on second guitar for Knife.

years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: Aztec Camera
years.h: Bob Dylan's Infidels sends Frame to Mark Knopfler
years.p: Living in New Orleans, Frame heard Infidels, saw Knopfler had produced it and wrote toward his sound. Knife reaches No. 14; its title track runs nearly nine minutes.
years.xp:
Frame told the Quietus he was "young and strident" and Knopfler was "very much into his own thing," but he learned a lot about guitar. He got to play Eric Clapton's acoustics, and Paul and Linda McCartney were recording in the same place.

In 2007 he explained the appeal to Edwyn Collins: while everyone else went digital, Knopfler's whole method was the right microphone, the right amp and the right desk.

years.src: Wikipedia: Aztec Camera
years.h: Brixton Academy raises £18,000 for the striking miners
years.p: Aztec Camera share the bill with Orange Juice, [[The Woodentops|90ae37a5-a693-4f81-893a-ca07ed365bdf]] and [[Everything but the Girl|959cf5bf-ee29-4af6-a85a-0b480181d988]]. The strike ends six weeks later.

years.src: Wikipedia: Aztec Camera · Wikipedia: Roddy Frame
years.h: Frame goes quiet in a wooden shack above Manchester
years.p: Owens is gone, and Frame spends the gap at Marple Bridge listening to the pop end of hip-hop: Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis, Cherrelle, the Force MDs, Alexander O'Neal.
years.xp: He said in 2014 he was moving even further from the British "indie ethic" in those three years. Working in a Goldmine was the first song that sounded the way he wanted.

eras.title: The pop end of hip-hop
eras.text: From Love on, Aztec Camera was Frame plus whoever he hired: American session players, a Boston dance producer, a Clash guitarist. The fans were puzzled, Warners was nervous, and it got him his biggest hits.

years.src: Wikipedia: Aztec Camera
years.h: Frame records in Boston and New York, against Warners' wishes
years.p: Marcus Miller, Steve Gadd and David Frank are among the session players. Frame said the audience was mystified and he was "too far gone" to care.

years.src: Wikipedia: Aztec Camera · Wikipedia: Aztec Camera discography
years.h: Love: Luther Vandross and Anita Baker are the reference points
years.p: The first three singles make little impression. Love still reaches No. 10 and gets a Best British Album nomination at the 1989 Brits.
years.xp: Asked on TV whether Love was middle of the road, Frame said: "Call it what you like. I don't really mind."

years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: Aztec Camera
yt: Somewhere in My Heart, official video
years.h: The song Frame wanted as a B-side goes to No. 3
years.p: Somewhere in My Heart, cut in Boston with Michael Jonzun, becomes the band's biggest hit. Frame called it "the runt of the litter."
years.xp: He told the Quietus that only Billy Bragg's charity single kept it from No. 1. In 2014 he admitted he'd thought it was an odd song that didn't fit Love: "I can't pick them."

years.h: Ruffy's last year behind Frame
years.p: Dave Ruffy, the drummer since 1982, is out; Kevin Smith and then Frank Tontoh take over the drums. Frame said in 1988 the line-up changes were about getting better, not blind ambition.

years.big: "You'll either sing on it, or you'll want to sue me."
years.src: Wikipedia: Aztec Camera
years.h: Good Morning Britain is written in 45 minutes
years.p: Frame's line to [[Mick Jones|01f8343c-06e2-4f05-a137-f8ea7efa85c4]] after writing a song that sounded like him. The Clash guitarist sings on it and it reaches No. 19.
years.xp:
The song came after a two- or three-hour talk with Jones in the canteen of a London rehearsal studio that Big Audio Dynamite and Aztec Camera were both using. The previous single, The Crying Scene, had stopped at No. 70, so it was taken as a comeback.

Jones toured with the band afterwards, including the Glasgow Barrowlands and the Ibiza Festival.

years.src: Wikipedia: Aztec Camera · Wikipedia: Aztec Camera discography
years.h: Stray pulls back from R&B toward guitars
years.p: AllMusic called it a loose cycle of folk, soul and pop. It reaches No. 22, and Frame contributes Do I Love You? to the AIDS benefit Red Hot + Blue the same year.

eras.title: Waiting for Sakamoto
eras.text: Frame waited out Ryuichi Sakamoto's schedule, made a record with him in New York, then handed the last Aztec Camera album to the producers of Madness. After that he dropped the name.

years.src: Wikipedia: Aztec Camera
years.h: Four weeks in New York with Ryuichi Sakamoto
years.p: Frame met Sakamoto in Ibiza after seeing him at London's Japan Festival. Dreamland reaches No. 21.
years.xp: Frame's New York routine, as he told The Independent's Giles Smith: studio from early afternoon to around 2am, a turkey sandwich from a deli off Times Square because it was open, a cab to the Mayflower Hotel, an hour of Shabba Ranks, bed.

years.src: Wikipedia: Aztec Camera · Wikipedia: Aztec Camera discography
years.h: Frestonia is the last record under the name
years.p: Produced by Clive Langer and Alan Winstanley, it peaks at No. 100. Frame leaves Warner and starts using his own name.

eras.title: Roddy Frame, under his own name
eras.text: Solo, Frame made four albums in sixteen years and stayed close to Edwyn Collins. The Aztec Camera catalogue kept coming back, once without him and once with him playing the debut start to finish.

years.src: Wikipedia: Roddy Frame
years.h: The North Star starts the solo run
years.p: Out on Independiente, it reaches No. 51. Surf follows in 2002 and Western Skies in 2006, both on Redemption.

years.src: Wikipedia: Aztec Camera
years.h: Edsel reissues all six albums without asking Frame
years.p: Frame tweeted that he wasn't involved and was talking to a "supercool US label" about a definitive set. That label was Domino, and only the debut came out.

years.cap: Frame at the Theatre Royal Drury Lane, London, 1 December 2013
years.src: Wikipedia: Aztec Camera · Wikipedia: Roddy Frame
years.h: Frame plays High Land, Hard Rain in London, Manchester and Glasgow
years.p: To get the old sound he swaps guitars at the top of every song, matching what he used in 1982. In Glasgow he adds Green Jacket Grey, cut from the original album.
years.xp: Campbell Owens came to the Glasgow show as a paying customer and thanked Frame backstage, which Frame said made the whole thing worthwhile. He told Monocle that revisiting the songs he wrote as a teenager turned out to be very moving, "even for an old cynic like me."

years.src: The Quietus · Wikipedia: Roddy Frame · Wikipedia: Aztec Camera
years.h: Seven Dials comes out on Edwyn Collins's label
years.p: Recorded at Collins's West Heath studio and released on AED, it reaches No. 50. Domino issues a 2CD High Land, Hard Rain in the US with notes by David Fricke.

years.src: Wikipedia: Aztec Camera
years.h: The Warner years get a nine-disc box
years.p: Backwards and Forwards collects everything from Knife to Frestonia, 1984 to 1995.
